chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from the man (Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him)) said: It is narrated from your fathers (peace be upon them) that they prohibited speaking about religion. Your followers who speak have interpreted that those who are not skilled in speaking about it were prohibited, but whoever is skilled was not prohibited. Is this as they interpreted or not? He (peace be upon him) wrote: Both the skilled and the unskilled should not speak about it, for indeed its sin is greater than its benefit.
ai.seo_question: Why are both experts and laypeople prohibited from speaking about religion according to Imam al-Kadhim?
ai.summary: Imam al-Kadhim (AS) refutes the Ta'wil (interpretation) of the Mu'tazilites and early theologians who argued that the prohibition on speaking about Allah's attributes applied only to those lacking expertise. He establishes a principle of caution (Ihtiyat), asserting that for both the expert and the novice, the risk of error and sin outweighs the benefit of discussion, thereby limiting speculative theology (Kalam) to preserve doctrinal purity.
